title: Connected Content Retriever: Dense Graph Edge Features Powering Pre-Ranking at LinkedIn
abstract: arXiv:2609.22441v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In large-scale recommendation systems like the LinkedIn Feed, content generated by a member's network (connections and follows) makes up over 70% of impressions and engagement. It is therefore essential that the pre-ranking layer forwards the best possible few hundred candidates to the ranking layer. LinkedIn's professional knowledge graph carries engagement signals across both the first degree network (connections and follows) and the second-degree network: posts that a 1st-degree connection reacted to, commented on or reshared but did not author (a.k.a. stranger viral). Due to this fan out, the resulting candidate index exceeds one billion; selection of activities from the viewer's network narrows it down to roughly tens of thousands of activities that must be scored within a 120 ms p99 latency budget. We present Connected Content Retriever (CC Retriever), a pre-ranking system that scores these candidates with a full deep ranking model

translated_title: 连接内容检索器：稠密图边特征驱动LinkedIn的预排序系统
translated_abstract: 在像LinkedIn Feed这样的大规模推荐系统中，由会员社交网络（连接和关注）生成的内容占曝光和互动总量的70%以上。因此，预排序层将最优的几百个候选内容传递给排序层至关重要。LinkedIn的专业知识图谱承载了跨越一度网络（连接和关注）和二度网络的互动信号：例如一度连接做出反应、评论或转发但并非其本人创作的帖子（即“陌生人病毒式传播”内容）。由于这种扇出效应，生成的候选索引超过十亿条；从查看者网络中筛选活动可将其缩小到大约数万条活动，而这些活动必须在120毫秒的p99延迟预算内完成评分。我们提出了连接内容检索器（CC Retriever），这是一个预排序系统，使用完整的深度排序模型对这些候选内容进行评分。
tldr: LinkedIn提出的连接内容检索器（CC Retriever）利用稠密图边特征，在120毫秒p99延迟预算内使用完整深度排序模型对来自一度和二度社交网络的数十亿候选内容进行预排序评分。
en_tdlr: LinkedIn's Connected Content Retriever (CC Retriever) leverages dense graph edge features to score billions of candidates from first- and second-degree social networks using a full deep ranking model within a 120 ms p99 latency budget.
